triples.relationship: a shepherd fails to seek, heal and protect the sheep
triples.rationale: Zechariah's coming shepherd neglects failing, scattered, broken and whole sheep and consumes the choice ones. Ezekiel likewise condemns shepherds who slaughter the fattened animal but fail to strengthen the weak, heal the sick, bind the broken or seek the lost. The detailed catalogue of neglected care closely corresponds.
triples.source_text: Look, I am raising up a shepherd over the land: he will certainly not attend to what is failing, seek what is scattered, heal what is broken or guide what is whole. He will devour the flesh of the choice ones and wrench their ankle bones.

target_units.text: Behold, you consume the milk, clothe yourselves with the wool and slaughter the fattened animal, but you do not feed My sheep.
You have not strengthened the weak, restored the sick to health, bound up the broken, brought back the wandering or sought the lost. You have worn down the strong with toil.

triples.relationship: a shepherding figure abandons the sheep
triples.rationale: Zechariah condemns those shepherding worthless things who abandon the sheep. Jesus' comparison likewise depicts a hired worker leaving the sheep and fleeing because he does not care for them. Both identify abandonment as failed care, without transferring the sword punishment to John's worker.
triples.source_text: Oh, you who shepherd worthless things and have abandoned the sheep! A sword against his arms and his right eye! His arm will utterly wither, and his right eye will be completely blinded.”

target_units.text: The hired worker, who is not a shepherd and does not own the sheep, sees the wolf coming and leaves the sheep and flees—and the wolf seizes them and scatters them—
because he is a hired worker and does not care for the sheep.

triples.relationship: the Creator of heaven and earth gives human spirit
triples.rationale: Zechariah introduces the Lord as stretching heaven, founding earth and forming the human spirit. Isaiah likewise names Him as maker of heaven, establisher of earth and giver of breath and spirit to people. The threefold creator description closely corresponds.
triples.source_text: An oracle of the Lord’s word concerning Israel. The Lord says—He who stretches out heaven, founds earth and forms a person’s spirit within him:

target_units.text: Thus says the Lord God, who made heaven and fixed it in place, established the earth and its contents, and gives breath to the people upon it and spirit to those treading it:

triples.relationship: Jerusalem surrounded and besieged
triples.rationale: Zechariah announces siege against Jerusalem alongside its shaking-entranceways image. Isaiah likewise describes a surrounding palisade and towers and names nations marching against Jerusalem. The connection concerns the explicitly besieged city, without replacing Zechariah's image with a cup.
triples.source_text: “Look, I am making Jerusalem like shaking entranceways for all the peoples around, and in Judea there will be a siege against Jerusalem.

target_units.text: I will surround you like David, set a palisade around you and set towers around you,
and your words will be humbled into the earth and sink into the earth. Your voice will be like those who speak from the earth, and your voice will weaken toward the ground.
The wealth of the ungodly will be like dust from a wheel, like drifting chaff, and it will be like a moment, immediately,
from the Lord Sabaoth. For there will be a visitation with thunder, earthquake and a great sound, a rushing storm and a consuming flame of fire.
Like someone dreaming in sleep will be the wealth of all nations who marched against Ariel, all who marched against Jerusalem, and all assembled against her and afflicting her.

triples.relationship: hostile nations gathered against Zion
triples.rationale: Zechariah says all earth's nations gather against Jerusalem. Micah likewise describes many nations gathered against Zion, rejoicing over her without understanding the Lord's purpose. Both present the hostile gathering around the named city, without importing injury to stone-lifters into Zechariah's trampled stone.
triples.source_text: On that day I will make Jerusalem a trampled stone for all the nations. Everyone trampling her will mock in mockery, and all the earth’s nations will gather against her.

target_units.text: Now many nations have gathered against you, saying, “We will rejoice over her, and our eyes will look upon Zion!”
But they did not know the Lord’s thought or understand His counsel, for He gathered them like sheaves of a threshing floor.

triples.relationship: the Lord strikes with madness, blindness and bewilderment
triples.rationale: Zechariah announces bewildered horses, maddened riders and blind horses among the peoples. Deuteronomy likewise names madness, blindness and mental bewilderment among the Lord's blows. The unusual cluster connects the warnings, with different recipients.
triples.source_text: On that day, says the Lord Almighty, I will strike every horse with bewilderment and its rider with madness. Over Judah’s house I will open My eyes, and I will strike all the peoples’ horses with blindness.

target_units.text: The Lord smite you with madness, and with blindness, and with bewilderment of mind.

triples.relationship: God's people pictured as fire consuming opposing peoples
triples.rationale: Zechariah likens Judah's commanders to a firebrand and flaming torch consuming surrounding peoples. Obadiah likewise pictures Jacob as fire, Joseph as flame and Esau as stubble consumed by them. Both use fire for the people overcoming opponents, while those opponents differ.
triples.source_text: On that day I will make Judah’s commanders of thousands like a firebrand among wood and a flaming torch among stalks. They will consume all the surrounding peoples to right and left, and Jerusalem will again dwell by herself.

target_units.text: The house of Jacob will be a fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau stubble. They will blaze against them and consume them, and there will be no bearer of fire in the house of Esau, because the Lord has spoken.

triples.relationship: the weak become strong in a battle setting
triples.rationale: Zechariah promises divine shielding so that the weak among Jerusalem's residents become like David's house. Joel likewise calls the powerless strong and the meek a fighter in the setting of gathered nations. Both express transformed weakness through battle strength, without equating all the participants.
triples.source_text: On that day the Lord will shield Jerusalem’s residents. The weak among them will be like David’s house on that day, and David’s house like God’s house, like the angel of the Lord before them.

target_units.text: Beat your plows into swords and your sickles into lances; let the powerless say, “I am strong!”
Assemble and enter, all surrounding nations, and gather there! Let the meek become a fighter!

triples.relationship: the hostile gathering against Jerusalem is frustrated
triples.rationale: Zechariah promises the Lord's removal of nations coming against Jerusalem. Isaiah describes the wealth of all nations marching against Jerusalem and Zion as a futile dream. Both overturn the hostile assembly's expected success through different images.
triples.source_text: On that day I will seek to remove all the nations coming against Jerusalem.

target_units.text: Like someone dreaming in sleep will be the wealth of all nations who marched against Ariel, all who marched against Jerusalem, and all assembled against her and afflicting her.

They will be like people drinking and eating in sleep; when they rise, their dream is futile. As a thirsty person dreams of drinking but wakes still thirsty, his soul having hoped in vain, so will be the wealth of all nations who marched against Mount Zion.

triples.relationship: God promises an outpouring of spirit
triples.rationale: Zechariah promises pouring a spirit of grace and compassion upon David's house and Jerusalem's residents. Joel likewise promises pouring out of God's Spirit upon all flesh, including slaves. Both expressly announce an outpouring, while recipients and stated effects differ.
triples.source_text: I will pour upon David’s house and Jerusalem’s residents a spirit of grace and compassion. They will look toward Me because they danced in mockery, and mourn over him as over a beloved one; they will suffer grief as over a firstborn.

target_units.text: “And it shall be after these things, that I will pour out of My Spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your elders shall dream dreams, and your young men shall see visions.
Even upon male slaves and female slaves in those days I will pour out of My Spirit.

triples.relationship: mourning compared with grief for a beloved one
triples.rationale: Zechariah describes mourning over someone as over a beloved one and grief as over a firstborn. Jeremiah likewise commands the daughter of the people to make a pitiful lament for a beloved one. The particular comparison of grief connects the passages without inserting piercing into Zechariah's mockery wording.
triples.source_text: I will pour upon David’s house and Jerusalem’s residents a spirit of grace and compassion. They will look toward Me because they danced in mockery, and mourn over him as over a beloved one; they will suffer grief as over a firstborn.

target_units.text: Daughter of My people, gird yourself with sackcloth; sprinkle yourself with ashes. Make mourning for yourself for a beloved one, a pitiful lament, because misery will suddenly come upon you.

triples.relationship: the removal and forgetting of idols' names
triples.rationale: Zechariah promises destruction of idols' names and the end of their remembrance. Hosea likewise promises removing the Baalim's names from the woman's mouth so they will no longer be remembered. Both explicitly remove the names as well as their remembrance.
triples.source_text: On that day, says the Lord, I will destroy the idols’ names from the land, and there will no longer be remembrance of them. I will remove the false prophets and the unclean spirit from the land.

target_units.text: I will remove the names of the Baalim from her mouth, and they will certainly no longer remember their names.

triples.relationship: a false prophet speaking in the Lord's name is declared liable to death
triples.rationale: Zechariah's parents tell their prophesying child he must not live because he spoke falsehood in the Lord's name. Deuteronomy likewise declares death for a prophet speaking in God's name words not commanded. The offense and stated consequence correspond; Zechariah subsequently describes binding feet rather than narrating execution.
triples.source_text: If a person still prophesies, his father and mother who begot him will say to him, ‘You shall not live, because you spoke falsehoods in the Lord’s name.’ His father and mother who begot him will bind his feet when he prophesies.

target_units.text: But the prophet who shall act ungodly, speaking in My name a word which I commanded him not to speak, or who shall speak in the name of other gods, that prophet shall die.

triples.relationship: family allegiance does not excuse religious deception
triples.rationale: Zechariah depicts parents opposing their own child for false prophecy in the Lord's name. Deuteronomy likewise prohibits protecting even close relatives who entice someone to other gods. Both place rejection of religious deception above family protection, while the offenses and prescribed actions differ.
triples.source_text: If a person still prophesies, his father and mother who begot him will say to him, ‘You shall not live, because you spoke falsehoods in the Lord’s name.’ His father and mother who begot him will bind his feet when he prophesies.

target_units.text: And if your brother, the son of your father or of your mother, or your son, or your daughter, or the wife of your bosom, or your friend who is as your own soul, entices you secretly, saying: Let us go and serve other gods, which you have not known, you nor your fathers,
of the gods of the nations round about you, whether near unto you or far from you, from one end of the earth unto the other,
you shall not consent unto him, neither shall you hearken unto him; neither shall your eye spare him, nor shall you yearn for him, nor conceal him.
You shall surely report him; your hands shall be first upon him to put him to death, and afterward the hands of all the people.
And they shall stone him with stones, and he shall die; for he sought to turn you away from the Lord your God, who brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.

triples.relationship: false visions expose prophets to judgment
triples.rationale: Zechariah describes prophets ashamed of their visions and explicitly says they lied. Ezekiel likewise confronts false visions and vain divinations and announces the prophets' exclusion from Israel's register and land. Both condemn the false visionary claim without assigning Zechariah's hairy skin to Ezekiel.
triples.source_text: On that day the prophets will be ashamed, each because of his vision when he prophesies; they will wear a hairy skin because they lied.

target_units.text: Have you not seen a false vision and spoken vain divinations?
Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: Because your words are false and your divinations vain, therefore behold, I am against you, says the Lord,

and I will stretch out My hand against the prophets who see false things and utter vain things. They will not belong to My people’s instruction, nor be written in the register of the house of Israel, nor enter Israel’s land. They will know that I am the Lord.

triples.relationship: contrasting denials of prophetic status with an agricultural occupation
triples.rationale: Zechariah's speaker denies being a prophet and identifies himself as a worker of the earth amid the exposure of lying prophets. Amos likewise says he was no prophet or prophet's son but a herder and fig worker, then recounts the Lord's call. The denial-and-occupation pattern is shared, while its contexts and force differ.
triples.source_text: He will say, ‘I am no prophet; I am a man who works the earth, because a man begot me from my youth.’

target_units.text: Amos answered Amaziah, “I was no prophet or prophet’s son, but a goat herder and one who scratches sycamore figs,
and the Lord took me from the sheep, and the Lord said to me, ‘Go, prophesy to My people Israel.’

triples.relationship: later Scripture quotation about striking the shepherd and dispersing sheep
triples.rationale: Zechariah commands a sword against shepherds and the striking of shepherds with sheep torn away. Jesus in Matthew introduces a written saying that the shepherd will be struck and the flock scattered, applying it to His disciples' coming failure. The shared action and flock consequence connect the texts while plural shepherds and singular shepherd remain distinct.
triples.source_text: Sword, awake against My shepherds, against the man who is My fellow citizen, says the Lord Almighty! Strike the shepherds and tear away the sheep; I will bring My hand against the shepherds.

target_units.text: Then Jesus said to them, “All of you will stumble because of Me this night, for it is written: ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.’
But after I am raised, I will go ahead of you to Galilee.”

triples.relationship: later written saying about the struck shepherd and scattered sheep
triples.rationale: Mark introduces Jesus' warning with a written saying about striking the shepherd and scattering the sheep. Zechariah likewise joins struck shepherds with sheep torn away. The correspondence is explicit in the actions, while Mark's singular shepherd and subsequent resurrection promise retain their own wording.
triples.source_text: Sword, awake against My shepherds, against the man who is My fellow citizen, says the Lord Almighty! Strike the shepherds and tear away the sheep; I will bring My hand against the shepherds.

target_units.text: Jesus said to them, “You will all stumble, because it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’
But after I am raised, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.”

triples.relationship: judgment represented through divided portions and a surviving remnant
triples.rationale: Zechariah divides the land's people into two parts that fail and a third that remains. Ezekiel divides symbolic hairs into quarters for judgment and gathers a few into his cloak. Both use measured portions to depict destruction and survival, without equating Zechariah's thirds with Ezekiel's quarters.
triples.source_text: Throughout the land, says the Lord, the two parts will be destroyed and fail, but the third will remain in it.

target_units.text: “And you, son of man, take a sword sharper than a barber’s razor. Obtain it for yourself and pass it over your head and your beard. Take a balance with weights and divide the hairs;

burn a quarter with fire inside the city when the days of siege are complete. Take a quarter and burn it up in its midst; cut down a quarter with the sword around it, and scatter a quarter to the wind. I will draw a sword after them.
Take a few of them in number and gather them into your cloak.
Take some of these again, cast them into the fire, and burn them in the fire. From it fire will go out. And you will say to the entire house of Israel,

triples.relationship: God's people tested by fire like silver
triples.rationale: Zechariah promises leading the remaining third through fire and refining it as silver. The psalm likewise tells God that He tested His people by fire as silver is tested and brought them through affliction. The refining comparison is explicit in both.
triples.source_text: I will lead the third through fire, refine them with fire as silver is refined and test them as gold is tested. He will call on My name, and I will listen to him and say, ‘This is My people,’ and he will say, ‘The Lord is my God.’”

target_units.text: For Thou didst test us, God; Thou didst try us by fire as silver is tried by fire.
Thou broughtest us into the trap; Thou didst place afflictions upon our back.
Thou madest human beings mount our heads; we passed through fire and water, and Thou broughtest us out to refreshment.

triples.relationship: purification of people compared with refining gold and silver
triples.rationale: Zechariah compares the surviving people's testing with the refining of silver and gold. Malachi likewise describes a smelting fire and purification of Levi's sons as gold and silver. Both apply metal refining to people, with distinct named groups.
triples.source_text: I will lead the third through fire, refine them with fire as silver is refined and test them as gold is tested. He will call on My name, and I will listen to him and say, ‘This is My people,’ and he will say, ‘The Lord is my God.’”

target_units.text: And who will endure the day of his entrance? Or who will stand at his appearance? For he enters like a smelting fire and like launderers’ herb.

He will sit, smelting and purifying as with silver and gold. He will cleanse the sons of Levi and melt them like gold and silver, and they will be those who bring a sacrifice to the Lord in righteousness.

triples.relationship: reciprocal declaration that God and His people belong to one another
triples.rationale: Zechariah ends the refining promise with God saying 'This is My people' and the people's response that the Lord is their God. Hosea likewise has God declare 'You are My people' and the answer 'Thou art the Lord my God.' The reciprocal formula directly corresponds.
triples.source_text: I will lead the third through fire, refine them with fire as silver is refined and test them as gold is tested. He will call on My name, and I will listen to him and say, ‘This is My people,’ and he will say, ‘The Lord is my God.’”

target_units.text: I will sow her for Myself upon the land, show mercy to Not Shown Mercy and say to Not My People, ‘You are My people.’ He will say, ‘Thou art the Lord my God!’”

triples.relationship: the Lord's approaching day in Jerusalem's judgment setting
triples.rationale: Zechariah announces days of the Lord before describing war against Jerusalem. Joel likewise announces the near Lord's day amid judgment and the Lord's voice from Jerusalem. Both locate the approaching divine day within the city's wider judgment and deliverance setting, with spoils specified in Zechariah.
triples.source_text: Look, days of the Lord are coming, and your spoils will be divided within you.

target_units.text: Sounds rang out in the Valley of Judgment, because the Lord’s day is near in the Valley of Judgment.
The sun and moon will grow dark, and the stars will sink their brightness.
The Lord will cry out from Zion and give His voice from Jerusalem; heaven and earth will shake. But the Lord will spare His people, and the Lord will strengthen the sons of Israel.

triples.relationship: same-book gathering of all nations against Jerusalem
triples.rationale: Chapter 14 announces the Lord gathering all nations against Jerusalem for war. Chapter 12 likewise describes all earth's nations gathering against her. The repeated gathering identifies a shared conflict setting without collapsing the different ensuing details.
triples.source_text: I will gather all the nations against Jerusalem for war. The city will be captured, the houses plundered and the women violated. Half the city will go into captivity, but the remnant of My people will certainly not be destroyed from the city.

target_units.text: On that day I will make Jerusalem a trampled stone for all the nations. Everyone trampling her will mock in mockery, and all the earth’s nations will gather against her.

triples.relationship: survivors remain in Jerusalem through the crisis
triples.rationale: Zechariah says that despite capture and captivity the remnant of God's people will not be destroyed from the city. Joel likewise promises one who escapes on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem amid the Lord's day. Both explicitly retain survival in that place.
triples.source_text: I will gather all the nations against Jerusalem for war. The city will be captured, the houses plundered and the women violated. Half the city will go into captivity, but the remnant of My people will certainly not be destroyed from the city.

target_units.text: Everyone who calls upon the Lord’s name will be saved, for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be one who escapes, as the Lord said, and bearers of good news whom the Lord has called.”
